feedback.problem:
Find the first two non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+5x+4{x}^{2}).$

$\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+5x+4{x}^{2})=$
{{field-1}}
$+\,\frac{65}{3}{x}^{3}+⋯$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, using the laws of logarithms, we observe that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+5x+4{x}^{2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((1+x)(1+4x)) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+4x).\end{aligned}
$$

For the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x),$ we recall the standard result

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x) & =x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

To obtain the expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+4x),$ we replace $x$ with $4x$ in the standard expansion:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+4x) & =(4x)-\frac{1}{2}(4x)^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(4x)^{3}-\frac{1}{4}(4x)^{4}+⋯ \\  & =4x-\frac{1}{2}(16{x}^{2})+\frac{1}{3}(64{x}^{3})-\frac{1}{4}(256{x}^{4})+⋯ \\  & =4x-8{x}^{2}+\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-64{x}^{4}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we add the two series to give the desired result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+5x+4{x}^{2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+4x) \\  & =(x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-⋯)+(4x-8{x}^{2}+\frac{64{x}^{3}}{3}-⋯) \\  & =(1+4)x+(-\frac{1}{2}-8){x}^{2}+(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{64}{3}){x}^{3}+⋯ \\  & =5x-\frac{17{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{65}{3}{x}^{3}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$
